clue.text: Model studies Shakespeare (nothing in it): his leader takes part in 3

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous early car, so model gives T
to study a subject at university is to read it

indicators.note: nothing goes in it, that is inside the poet's nickname

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard
nothing is zero, the letter O
his refers back to Shakespeare, whose leading letter is S

explanation.surface: A model studies Shakespeare's works, and the playwright's leading lady joins in an amateur production.
explanation.walkthrough: '(nothing in it)' puts O inside THE BARD to make THE BOARD; 'his' means Shakespeare's, so his leader is S. 3 is PLAY, so taking part in one is acting on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading the boards is the idiom for acting on stage, which is taking part in a play.

clue.text: Holidaying with long-haired weirdies in bars, not stressed

parts.note: someone holidaying is off work
beats, or beatniks, were the long-haired bohemians of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A holiday spent with long-haired eccentrics drinking in bars sounds relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs, but it is musical bars, divisions of a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeats are the unaccented beats within a musical bar, the ones not given stress.

clue.text: Hamlet's thing to do with 25

definitions.meaning: Hamlet says 'the ... the thing wherein I'll catch the conscience of the king'
25 is PIPE, and what you do with a pipe is perform music on it

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet calls a drama 'the thing', and you perform music on a pipe, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Thinking of avoiding the unpleasant spectacles, am I?

indicators.note: the question mark signals that the abbreviated spectacles and the words am I must be rearranged

parts.note: spectacles are informally called specs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are just ignoring unpleasantness by refusing to wear glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectacles must first be shortened to SPECS, then shuffled with AM I; the only signal is the closing question mark. 'Unpleasant' nods to Shaw's Plays Unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is a habit of mind that retreats into fantasy to avoid unpleasant reality.

clue.text: Operation with 27 in 13 3 for 17 acrosses

definitions.meaning: a Caesarean section is often shortened informally to ...
... and Cleopatra is one of Shaw's Three Plays for Puritans

explanation.definitionFit: A Caesarean birth is informally a Caesar, and Shaw paired the Roman general with Cleopatra in a play.

clue.text: Noisy bird, with possibly unfinished crest, half American!

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged some other way
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half takes the first four of the eight letters of American

explanation.surface: A loud bird with a scruffy crest turns out to be half American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts CREST to CRES, which 'possibly' rearranges to SCRE; 'half' of American gives AMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Screamers are large South American waterbirds named for their loud trumpeting calls.

clue.text: Quarter note?

definitions.meaning: quarters are lodgings, especially for soldiers
an old word for a short letter or note

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are billeted in quarters, and a billet-doux is a love note, the billet being the letter.

clue.text: Traditional feast of Wagner's work gets us up into its sequel

indicators.note: into says the work and the turned-up pronoun go inside the following day

parts.note: its refers to Sunday, the day of the feast, and the day that follows it is Monday
Wagner's great opera cycle is known as The Ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traditional festival features Wagner's operas, and we are hoisted into the follow-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns US round, and the pieces go 'into' the day after Sunday: 'its' refers to the feast day itself, so its sequel is the next day.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothering Sunday is the traditional British Lent festival, now Mother's Day, once a feast day of the Church.

clue.text: Weaving fibres conceal small boy, one with big flowers

indicators.note: the fibres conceal the boy by wrapping round him

parts.note: raffia is a palm fibre used for weaving baskets and mats
Les is a shortened form of the boy's name Leslie

explanation.surface: Woven fibres hide a little boy who is carrying a huge bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' means the name is cut short: LES for Leslie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafflesia is a parasitic plant famous for having the largest single flowers in the world.

clue.text: Letters from Athens read out in capital

indicators.note: read out says the letter names are pronounced, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: chi and rho are two letters of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Correspondence from Athens is read out to an audience somewhere in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: CHI RHO, said as 'kye roe', sounds like the Egyptian city. 'Letters' looks like correspondence but means alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Wood, a funny man about what he was

indicators.note: about says the rearranged man goes round the next piece
funny means the letters of the word are made odd, mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
every man was once a boy

explanation.surface: A comedian is talked about in terms of what he used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' scrambles the man, and 'about' wraps him round what every man once was. 'Funny man' looks like a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Amboyna is a decorative hardwood from the East Indies, named after the island of Ambon.

clue.text: The last sort of tax to be unveiled?

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so the words are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which kind of tax will be the final one announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' looks like a vague phrase but tells you to rearrange THE LAST. The question mark marks the definition as playful: a stealth tax is one never openly unveiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealth tax is one raised quietly, so taxing by stealth means the levy is never properly revealed.

clue.text: Wood cutter when drunk?

indicators.note: when drunk says the word is spoken with a slurred s, as a tipsy person would say it

parts.note: a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: A woodcutter is handling his saw while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs 'saw' into a 'sh' sound. The answer is also the playwright behind the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw is an old and dialect word for a small wood or thicket.

clue.text: English painter enters American joint for a little measure

indicators.note: the painter enters the joint, going inside it

parts.note: a mitre joint is spelt miter in American English
John Crome was an English landscape painter of the Norwich School

explanation.surface: An English artist walks into an American bar for a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a bar, but it is a carpentry joint; 'measure' tempts as a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A micrometer is a gauge for measuring very small distances, and also names a tiny unit of length.

clue.text: Pious people faint after Shia's conversion

indicators.note: after puts the word for faint behind the converted letters
conversion means the letters are changed into another form

parts.note: taken as written; the 's is only the link to conversion
a faint light is dim

explanation.surface: Devout believers grow weak after a Shia Muslim changes faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' looks religious, but it is the anagram signal; 'after' puts the word for faint at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hasidim are a strictly devout movement within Orthodox Judaism; the singular is Hasid.

clue.text: Learner of 26, 13 3 for 17 acrosses

definitions.meaning: a pupil or follower who learns from a teacher
The Devil's ... is one of Shaw's Three Plays for Puritans

explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower learning from a master, and Shaw wrote The Devil's Disciple.

clue.text: Pious person's joke about educated woman

indicators.note: the joke goes about, that is round, the woman

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
Rita is the heroine of Willy Russell's play Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A devout person makes a joke about a woman who has had schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'educated woman' points to Educating Rita, a British play and film about a working-class woman going to university.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is a person of strict religious and moral principles.

clue.text: Chosen article being inserted, lost head

indicators.note: being inserted says the article goes inside the word for chosen

parts.note: something chosen is picked
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A selected newspaper article goes in, and someone loses their head over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose your head is to stop thinking calmly, which is exactly what someone who panicked did.

clue.text: Still climbing, holding by oneself a social gathering

indicators.note: holding says the reversed word holds the next piece inside it
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: still, as in 'still here', means yet
someone apart is set aside on their own

explanation.surface: Still going upwards while holding on alone, someone heads for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns YET into TEY, which holds APART: TE-APART-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a social event where guests gather for afternoon tea.

clue.text: See 24
Come into prominence somewhere near river

indicators.note: read as some where: some says only a run of letters inside the following words is wanted

explanation.surface: A place near a river becomes famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhere' must be split: 'some' signals a run of letters inside 'near river', and 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having arrived means having become successful and recognised, as in 'she has finally arrived'.

clue.text: Choose to upset leaders of science, for one

parts.note: to choose is to opt

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone chooses to upset the leading scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' signals the shortening of science to its abbreviation SCI, which is then turned up. 'For one' means 'such as science', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Optics is the branch of physics studying light, so it is one science among many.

clue.text: Drink like a fish?

definitions.meaning: A well-known brand of British pale ale
a fish, here comically described as fish-like

explanation.definitionFit: Bass is both a classic British ale and a species of sea fish, giving both readings.

clue.text: Tune to get higher, but end with a drop

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
to lift is to raise or get higher

explanation.surface: A singer is told to lift the melody higher but finish with a fall in pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a melody rising and falling; the definition is loose, since supplies carried by air often end up dropped by parachute.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift transports supplies by aircraft, often finishing with a parachute drop to those on the ground.

clue.text: Follow acknowledgement in money before spring being converted in 13 3 for 17 acrosses

parts.note: to cap a remark is to follow it with a better one
ta is British slang for thanks
taken as written
brass is northern English slang for money
to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: Thanks follow a payment made before spring, as someone undergoes a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The play's full title is Captain Brassbound's Conversion, so 'being converted' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Brassbound's Conversion is the Shaw play whose hero is converted, one of his Three Plays for Puritans.

clue.text: Conductor of "Water Music" hence

definitions.meaning: a tube carrying water through a building is a conductor of water
music comes from blowing into a wind instrument of this name

explanation.definitionFit: A pipe carries water through plumbing, and a pipe is also a simple wind instrument making music.

clue.text: Was coming back to cook

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to have lived is to have existed, to have been

explanation.surface: Someone was returning home in order to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns LIVED into the cooking word.
explanation.definitionFit: To devil food is to cook it with hot spices, as in devilled kidneys.

clue.text: Work — artwork — in lacework requires needlewoman

indicators.note: the work pieces go inside the rearranged lace

parts.note: split as lace plus work, work signalling that the letters of lace are rearranged
op is short for opus, a musical work
split as art plus work, work signalling that the letters of art are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making a piece of artwork from lace demands a skilled seamstress.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'artwork' and 'lacework' split into a word plus 'work', which rearranges it; 'in' puts the work pieces inside the rearranged lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's Needle is the obelisk on London's Victoria Embankment, so the queen is jokingly a woman with a needle.
